newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German generals to be jailed for wall deaths.
newsitem.headline: East German generals to be jailed for wall deaths.

text.p: The German supreme court on Thursday upheld a Berlin court verdict that six former East German generals were guilty of ordering border guards to shoot refugees trying to escape to the West.

The court rejected the ex-generals' constitutional complaint against their convictions. They had argued they were carrying out orders by telling troops to set up mine fields and automatic shooting devices and giving shoot-to-kill orders.
More than 800 people died along the Cold War-era barriers trying to flee the communist East.

The Berlin court had sentenced the six officers to between three years and three months and more than six years in jail last year for 15 counts of manslaughter and attempted manslaughter between 1980 and 1989.
The Federal Constitutional Court, the highest court in the land, said in its ruling the generals had placed the state's interests above East German citizens' "right to life".

"This disregard for basic human rights, which were also recognised in East Germany, to support the reckless achievement of political goals was...the worst kind of injustice," the court said in its judgement.
The judge said border guards should have known that the killing of defenceless refugees was illegal, despite political indoctrination in the former communist state.

Klaus-Dieter Baumgarten, a former East Germany deputy defence minister, received the longest prison sentence of six and a half years because he was directly implicated in the deaths of 11 people trying to escape into the West.
He and four subordinate generals as well as the general in charge of border security were convicted.
Dozens of lower-ranking border guards have already been convicted of murder, but given suspended sentences.

Four of the generals accepted partial responsibility for killings at the Berlin Wall in a letter in 1991 to the Speaker of the German parliament, Rita Suessmuth, and asked for the border guards who fired the fatal shots to be excused.
